intended_object: The forgetful map sending a unitary multiplicative weight on ideals of 𝓞_K to its underlying arithmetic function: the complex-valued function on nonzero ideals I ↦ χ(I). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation ("passage to the general carrier").
explanation: UnitaryIdealWeight K is a subtype of MultiplicativeIdealWeight K: weights χ with ‖χ 𝔭‖ = 1 at every prime 𝔭 outside χ's bad primes. The definition takes the underlying weight χ.1 and applies MultiplicativeIdealWeight.toIdealArithmeticFunction, which is IdealArithmeticFunction.restrict χ, i.e. I ↦ χ I on (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰. The target type IdealArithmeticFunction K is (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰ → ℂ. So the result is exactly the restriction of the weight to nonzero ideals, as the docstring says. The unitarity condition plays no role in the values, which is right for a forgetful map. The setting is the one used throughout the module (a number field K and ideals of 𝓞 K), and the definition adds no assumptions of its own beyond those of the types it acts on. Mathlib has no counterpart because it does not have these weight types. This is essentially a coercion and could be seen as an implementation detail. It is classed as faithful because it is the standard step of viewing a character or weight on ideals as an arithmetic function on nonzero ideals, the input to its Dirichlet series.
